mainTopic: Testing עולא's rule that a tree's roots draw from 16 אמות: the math of a בית סאה and challenges from the laws of ביכורים
overview: עולא said a tree's roots draw nourishment from 16 אמות around it. The גמרא first tests this against a משנה about three trees in a בית סאה: dividing 2,500 square אמות among them gives each about 833⅓, but 16 אמות on every side makes a 32×32 square of 1,024. The גמרא answers that עולא rounded (לא דק), then objects that rounding is only accepted when it leads to strictness. It explains that the roots spread in a circle, not a square, which cuts the area to 768. Now עולא's 16 is about half an אמה short of the exact figure, so his rounding falls on the strict side and is accepted. The גמרא then brings two משניות about bringing and reciting over ביכורים: one about a buyer of a tree and its land, and one about a buyer of trees in someone else's field. Both seem to allow any amount of land. Each time it answers that the buyer owns 16 אמות. Finally it starts a third challenge from רבי עקיבא, who says any amount of land is obligated in פאה and ביכורים. That quote continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The math of three trees in a בית סאה doesn't match עולא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא divides the 2,500 square אמות of a בית סאה among three trees and gets 833⅓ each. That is less than the area עולא's 16 אמות would give.
steps.simpleTranslation: The whole בית סאה is plowed for the three trees. How much is that? 2,500 square אמות. How much does each tree get? 833⅓. But עולא's amount is still bigger!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a משנה about three trees in a בית סאה and runs the numbers. The result clashes with עולא's 16 אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If each tree needs only 833⅓ square אמות, its roots reach a shorter distance than עולא claimed. Sixteen אמות in every direction makes a 32×32 square, which is 1,024 square אמות. So עולא's figure looks too large.

keyTerms.meaning: An area of land 50 by 50 אמות (2,500 square אמות)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't compare 16 with 833 directly. 16 is a distance in each direction, and 833⅓ is an area. The fair comparison is 1,024 square אמות against 833⅓.

phrases.english: a בית סאה for their sake.
phrases.notes: This is the end of the משנה quoted just before: with three trees in a בית סאה, the whole area is plowed for them.

phrases.english: How much is that?
2,500 square cubits;
how much reaches each one?
833 and a third;
Still, עולא's amount is greater!
phrases.notes: 16 אמות on every side of the tree makes a 32×32 square, which comes to 1,024.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the challenge to עולא that began before this section by finishing the quote from the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's claim that roots reach 16 אמות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה implies each tree uses 833⅓ square אמות, which is less than the 1,024 that 16 אמות in each direction would give.

steps.title: עולא was not being exact
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that עולא gave a rounded number.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends עולא by saying his 16 אמות was a rough figure, not an exact measurement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The math does not have to match perfectly, because עולא rounded. The problem is that this answer will be questioned right away in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: He was not precise; he rounded

phrases.english: He was not precise.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: עולא's 16 אמות must exactly match the משנה's numbers.
steps.terutzMaskana: עולא gave an approximate number, so a gap is acceptable.

steps.title: Rounding is only accepted when it leads to strictness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: we only say לא דק when the rounding makes the law stricter, but here it would make it more lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fine, we say 'he was not precise' when it leads to strictness. But do we say 'he was not precise' when it leads to leniency?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rounding answer. It says rounding is allowed only when it makes things stricter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rounding up to 16 makes the root zone bigger than the real one. That would treat trees as drawing from a neighbor's field when they really don't, so their owner would be exempted from bringing ביכורים. That is a leniency. A rule of thumb is only acceptable when its error falls on the safe side, so this rounding seems unacceptable.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a general rule: an approximate number is accepted only when its error leads to strictness.

phrases.english: Granted we say 'he was not precise' toward stringency;
toward leniency, do we say 'he was not precise'?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rounding answer of step 2.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Rounding is acceptable only when it leads to strictness. Here עולא's larger number would lead to leniency.

steps.title: The roots spread in a circle, not a square
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the 16 אמות describes a circle around the tree, which covers less area than a square.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you think we are talking about a square?! We are talking about a circle!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the challenge assumed the wrong shape. The roots spread out in a circle around the tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A circle with a radius of 16 covers less area than a 32×32 square. That shrinks עולא's area so much that it drops below the משנה's 833⅓. So עולא's figure is no longer too large, and the leniency problem goes away. The next step does the exact math.

phrases.english: Do you think we are speaking of a square?!
We are speaking of a circle!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem from step 3 by redefining the shape of the root area.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting an assumption: the area is a circle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 16 אמות means a 32×32 square of 1,024 square אמות.
steps.terutzMaskana: 16 אמות means a circle, which has a smaller area.

steps.title: Even with a circle, half an אמה is left over
steps.stepSummary: Taking away a quarter gives 768 square אמות. That is now less than 833⅓, so the exact distance should be about 16½ אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, by how much is a square bigger than a circle? By a quarter. So 768 remain. But there is still half an אמה left over!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא recalculates with a circle and finds the numbers still don't match exactly. Now עולא's figure comes out slightly too small.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Removing the square's extra quarter from 1,024 leaves 768, which is less than the משנה's 833⅓. To match the משנה, the distance would have to be about 16½ אמות. So עולא is still not exact.

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּדֵי כַּמָּה מְרוּבָּע יוֹתֵר עַל הָעִיגּוּל –
phrases.english: Now, by how much is a square greater than a circle?
A quarter;
phrases.notes: The square is bigger by a quarter of the circle, so the circle is three-quarters of the square.

phrases.aramaic: פָּשׁוּ לְהוּ שְׁבַע מְאָה וְשִׁתִּין וּתְמָנְיָא;
phrases.english: 768 remain;
there still remains half a cubit!
phrases.notes: To reach the משנה's 833⅓, the distance would have to be about 16½ אמות instead of 16.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדֵי כַּמָּה מְרוּבָּע יוֹתֵר עַל הָעִיגּוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the circle answer of step 4 with exact math.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the circle reading makes עולא fit the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A circle gives 768, which is below 833⅓, so the correct distance would be about 16½ אמות, not 16.

steps.title: עולא rounded, and on the strict side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that this half-אמה gap is what לא דק meant, and here the rounding leads to strictness.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is what we meant by 'he was not precise,' and he was imprecise toward strictness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the discussion. The small gap is exactly the rounding it mentioned earlier, and this time the rounding falls on the strict side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we use a circle, עולא's 16 is a little smaller than the exact 16½. According to the גמרא, that kind of rounding leads to strictness, so it is acceptable under the rule from step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: That is, this is what is meant

steps.whatToRemember: עולא's 16 אמות is a circle around the tree. The exact figure is about 16½, and the גמרא accepts the rounding because it leads to strictness.

phrases.english: That is what 'he was not precise' means –
and he was imprecise toward stringency.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the leftover half-אמה from step 5 by bringing back the rounding answer of step 2, now in a form that passes the test of step 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: עולא's 16 אמות is a slightly rounded-down circle radius (exact is about 16½), and rounding that leads to strictness is acceptable.

steps.title: Challenge from a buyer of a tree and its land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites a משנה that a person who buys a tree with its land brings ביכורים and recites. It suggests this means any amount of land, which would clash with עולא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: One who buys a tree and its land brings ביכורים and recites the פסוקים. Doesn't this mean even a tiny amount of land?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to attack עולא's rule. It suggests the משנה lets a person recite over his tree even if he owns only a tiny bit of land with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to עולא, a tree feeds from 16 אמות of ground around it. If the owner has only a tiny bit of land, the tree is feeding from ground that is not his, so how can he recite about 'the land You gave me'? The משנה seems to allow it anyway, which challenges עולא.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear — the גמרא is bringing a source to prove or challenge something
He brings ביכורים and recites the פסוקים
Any amount at all, even a tiny bit
First fruits brought to the בית המקדש

steps.confusionAlert: Bringing ביכורים and reciting over them are two separate things. Someone can bring the fruit without being allowed to recite, so 'brings and recites' is the full level.

phrases.english: Come and hear: One who buys a tree and its land
brings [first fruits] and recites.
phrases.notes: He recites the ביכורים פסוקים, דברים 26:5–11.

phrases.english: What, is it not [talking about] any amount [of land]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the math of עולא's 16 אמות, the גמרא now tests the rule against a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's rule that a tree draws its food from 16 אמות around it
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a tiny amount of land is enough to recite, then the tree feeding from a neighbor's ground does not matter, which goes against עולא.

steps.title: The משנה means he bought 16 אמות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the challenge: the משנה is talking about someone who bought 16 אמות of land around the tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: No; it means he bought 16 אמות of land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the challenge. It says the משנה is talking about a buyer who owns 16 אמות around the tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'and its land' do not have to mean a tiny amount. If he owns the full 16 אמות, the tree feeds only from his ground, so he may recite, and עולא stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A cubit, a measure of length

phrases.english: No; [he bought] sixteen cubits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 by limiting the case of the משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the reading that the משנה means any amount of land.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The challenge assumed 'its land' means a tiny amount, but it can mean the full 16 אמות.

steps.title: Challenge from a buyer of three trees
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites a משנה: a person who bought two trees in someone else's field brings but does not recite. So with three trees he brings and recites. Doesn't that mean with any amount of land?
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If he bought two trees in his friend's field, he brings but does not recite. So with three trees, he brings and recites. Doesn't this mean with any amount of land?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second משנה to challenge עולא. It reads that a buyer of three trees may recite, and suggests this works even with only a little land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says two trees are not enough to recite, so we learn that three trees are enough. The גמרא suggests that three trees count with any amount of land, even though the trees feed from the friend's ground. That would go against עולא.

keyTerms.meaning: Belonging to his friend (someone else's field)
He brings ביכורים but does not recite
This implies — the גמרא is learning from what the משנה did not say

phrases.english: Come and hear: If he bought two trees
in [the field] of his friend,
he brings but does not recite.
This implies that [with] three, he brings and recites;
What, is it not [with] any amount [of land]?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: קָנָה שְׁנֵי אִילָנוֹת בְּתוֹךְ שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge against עולא, built the same way as step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's rule that a tree draws its food from 16 אמות around it
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An inference from the משנה suggests three trees with any amount of land are enough to recite, which ignores the trees feeding from the friend's ground.

steps.title: Here too it means 16 אמות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects this challenge the same way: the case is where he owns 16 אמות of land.
steps.simpleTranslation: No; here too it means 16 אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the second challenge with the same answer as before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three-tree case is also explained as someone who owns 16 אמות around the trees. So the משנה does not prove that any amount of land is enough, and עולא's rule survives.

phrases.aramaic: לָא; הָכָא נָמֵי שֵׁשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה אַמָּה.
phrases.english: No; here too [he bought] sixteen cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא; הָכָא נָמֵי שֵׁשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה אַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9 using the same answer given in step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the reading that three trees with any amount of land are enough.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The inference assumed any amount of land, but the case can be one where he owns 16 אמות.
steps.whatToRemember: Both משניות about reciting over ביכורים are explained as cases where the buyer owns 16 אמות, so neither one disproves עולא.

steps.title: Challenge from רבי עקיבא: any amount of land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a third challenge: רבי עקיבא says any amount of land is obligated in פאה and ביכורים, and a פרוזבול can be written on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי עקיבא says: Land of any size is obligated in פאה and ביכורים, and one may write a פרוזבול based on it,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a third challenge against עולא from a statement of רבי עקיבא. The quote continues past this section, so the challenge is only being set up here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the source says outright 'any amount of land,' so it cannot easily be read as 16 אמות. If even a tiny piece of land brings ביכורים, the trees on it feed from other people's ground, which seems to go against עולא.

keyTerms.meaning: A great תנא whose opinion is quoted in the משנה
Land of any size, even a tiny piece
The corner of the field left for the poor
A document that keeps שמיטה from canceling a loan

phrases.english: Come and hear: Rabbi Akiva says:
Land of any amount
is obligated in pe'a and in first fruits,
and one may write a prosbol on it,
phrases.notes: A פרוזבול can only be written for a borrower who owns land, and even a tiny piece counts. The quote keeps going after this.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: קַרְקַע כׇּל שֶׁהוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third challenge against עולא, this time from a source that says 'any amount' outright.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's rule that a tree draws its food from 16 אמות around it
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי עקיבא says even a tiny piece of land brings ביכורים, which suggests it does not matter that the trees feed from neighboring ground.
